text:
ACME Support: Hey team — starting ~03:40 UTC ACME-Corp reported a large number of 429s on /v1/generate and intermittent timeouts. They say some requests completed with partial output, others were cut off. Their app is showing spike in client-side retries.

Sara (Support): Noted. Can you drop a few example request_ids + the API key suffix (first 8 chars) so we can correlate? Also which region/route/model?

ACME Support: Example request ids: r_6a3f2b1, r_b9c8d7e, r_72f3a11. API key suffix: ab12cd34. Route: /v1/generate (public). Model: rdx-large-v1. Region: us-west-2. Time window: 03:38 — 03:56 UTC.

Dan (Metrics): Got it — I'll pull throttle + latency metrics. Quick queries I'm running: 

PromQL (throttle rate by customer/route/model):
```
sum by(customer_id, route, model) (increase(redwood_api_responses_total{status="429"}[5m]))
/ sum by(customer_id, route, model) (increase(redwood_api_responses_total[5m]))
```

ClickHouse to get attribution (last 1h):
```
SELECT customer_id, route, model, countIf(status=429) AS throttles, count() AS total,
       round(throttles*1.0/total, 4) AS throttle_rate
FROM requests
WHERE ts >= now() - 3600
GROUP BY customer_id, route, model
ORDER BY throttle_rate DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Dan (Metrics): Early result — ACME-Corp shows throttle_rate ~0.9% on /v1/generate against model rdx-large-v1 in the time window. Total requests ~27k for that hour. There's a noticeable spike in latency (p50 -> 320ms to 1.2s, p95 -> 800ms to 3.1s) concurrent with the throttles.

Ingrid (Oncall): I'm tailing the request logs for the request ids. Here's a typical server response header we see on 429s: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 60000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 167
content-type: application/json
```
Body: {"error":"quota_exhausted","message":"burst window exceeded"} 

Priya (SRE): That header pattern suggests per-customer quota exhaustion (global token budget + burst window). Two hypotheses: 1) ACME hit their sustained quota and then exhausted burst credits, or 2) a bug in the burst accounting made remaining go to zero prematurely. Also check billing/usage reconciliation — if a billing flag flipped it can shrink quota instantly.

Sara (Support): ACME says they did a deploy at ~03:35 locally that increased request concurrency (feature flag changed batching from 8 -> 1). Could explain 3x request count. Can we confirm per-route token counts to see if token vs request volume caused burst depletion?

Dan (Metrics): On it. Querying token usage and burst credits spent: 
```
-- approximate tokens per response + request
SELECT customer_id, sum(tokens_used) AS tokens, sum(burst_charged) AS burst_spent
FROM token_usage
WHERE ts >= now() - 7200
AND customer_id = 'acme-corp'
GROUP BY customer_id;
```

Dan (Metrics): Results — tokens increased ~2.8x after 03:35, burst_spent jumped and exhausted ACME's burst allowance at 03:43. That lines up.

ACME Support: Is there an alert for when burst allowance hits 0? We didn't get notified.

Priya (SRE): There is an alert but it's scoped to reserved capacity customers only. Hosted customers didn't have a customer-level burst exhaustion alert. That's a gap.

Ingrid (Oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily raise ACME's burst allowance (manual override), 2) throttle them to a lower per-second rate (graceful), 3) ask the app team to rollback batching change. Which do you want?

ACME Support: We applied a hotfix to revert batching at 04:02 UTC. We still want to understand the observability gaps so we can prevent repeats.

Sara (Support): Thanks. For root-cause and follow-up: can we add a dashboard panel that attributes 429s to customer_id + route + model, and an alert when throttle_rate > 0.5% for any customer over 5m? Add a runbook entry for support on how to quickly check per-customer burst credits and perform manual override.

Dan (Metrics): Agree. Proposed Grafana panel (PromQL):
```
sum by(customer_id, route, model) (increase(redwood_api_responses_total{status="429"}[5m]))
/ sum by(customer_id, route, model) (increase(redwood_api_responses_total[5m]))
```
Visualization: heatmap table, auto-sort by throttle_rate desc. Link placeholder: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/quil/quotas?orgId=1

Dan (Metrics): Also adding a small metric to logs for attribution: log label "quota_bucket" and include current burst_remaining. That will make Correlate queries much faster.

Priya (SRE): Alert text draft: "High throttle rate detected — {customer_id}/{route}/{model} throttle_rate > 0.5% over 5m". Severity: P2, notify support + oncall + account owner. Runbook step 1: check burst_remaining and billing flags; step 2: apply manual override if customer impacted and on-call approves; step 3: suggest app rollback or apply per-route rate limiting.

Ingrid (Oncall): I pushed a short-lived manual override for ACME (added 10k burst credits) at 04:15 UTC. Throttles dropped to ~0.02% by 04:20. No further user-visible errors reported.

Sara (Support): ACME confirms errors stopped after the revert and your override — thanks.

ACME Support: Can you also provide a quick repro that we can run in staging to exercise the quota logic so our infra team can validate?

Dan (Metrics): Repro script (small load test):
```
# fire 200 concurrent short generation requests against /v1/generate
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-<FIRST8>..." \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rdx-large-v1","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}' &
done
wait
```
Expected: if you sustain > X requests/s you'll see x-rate-limit-remaining hit 0 and subsequent 429s with body {"error":"quota_exhausted","message":"burst window exceeded"}.

Priya (SRE): Add these logs to a staging run and inspect burst_remaining in the response header or in request logs. New SRE task: add header x-burst-remaining and include it in access logs for hosted customers (PR filed).

Dan (Metrics): I filed dashboard + alert PR: https://git.internal/redwood/monitoring/pulls/219 — includes attribution panels, a per-customer throttle-rate alert, and a quick link to the manual override page in the account console.

Priya (SRE): Follow-ups: 1) extend burst exhaustion alert to hosted plans (owner: Priya), 2) add burst_remaining header to responses (owner: Dan), 3) add runbook + support playbook (owner: Sara). Target ETA: 48h for alerts + runbook, 72h for header and dashboard baked.

Ingrid (Oncall): Closing immediate incident — ACME recovered. Logging this as an internal post-incident ticket: INTERNAL-1367 — "hosted-customer burst exhaustion: observability & alerts gap".

Sara (Support): I'll send ACME a short postmortem and include mitigation steps + suggested app changes (gradual backoff, client-side retry jitter, reduce per-request tokens).

ACME Support: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick response and suggestions. Please cc our account rep on the postmortem.

ops-bot: Incident CLOSED by Ingrid at 04:31 UTC :white_check_mark:
metrics-bot: alert fired: quota_throttle_rate_high (acme-corp / /v1/generate) at 03:44 UTC — auto-resolved at 04:18 UTC

---

Action items (summary):
- Priya: widen alerting for burst exhaustion to hosted customers (48h)
- Dan: add x-burst-remaining header + dashboard panels (72h)
- Sara: author support runbook + customer PM (48h)
- Team: consider a per-route / per-model soft-limit to avoid global burst drain (design discussion)

Follow-up thread: please post PR links and the final postmortem here when ready.
